content.text: {"count": 2, "rationale": "Deploying mfa:admin and mfa:dbadmin together blocks exfiltration. (1) Why 2 is enough: mfa:admin blocks auth_dc and auth_adfs, so admin_dc and admin_adfs can never be reached. With no admin_dc or admin_adfs, mfa:dbadmin blocks auth_db, auth_fileserver and auth_backup. No other technique gives a foothold on db, fileserver or backup, and every exfiltrate technique needs admin on one of them. So exfiltration is impossible. (2) Why 1 is not enough: Phishing is always available and gives foothold_workstation and stolen_user. mfa:user does not stop auth_appserver, auth_apiserver or auth_ciserver, because a workstation foothold bypasses it. No patch blocks the escalation paths. Each single control fails: segmented alone fails because escalate_workstation gives admin_workstation, which lets pivot_internal succeed. mfa:admin alone fails because auth_ciserver, kerberoast and escalate_ciserver give leak_secrets_ciserver, which yields stolen_dbadmin; auth_db then works and escalate_db leads to exfiltrate_db. mfa:dbadmin alone fails because kerberoast gives stolen_admin, auth_dc and escalate_dc give admin_dc, and admin_dc bypasses the dbadmin MFA. Any other single control leaves these same paths open. (3) Other minimum sets: segmented plus patched:workstation plus patched:laptop also works, but it uses 3 controls."}
